review_method: Assistant inspected eight sampled frames per case: 0,11,22,34,45,57,68,80. Not exhaustive frame review.

VP002.observation: Scene and both people remain recognizable. Wood is already bowed initially; hands move upward while the bowed object changes little. Hand/arm-to-object contact appears inconsistent in middle/later samples. The requested bending process is not clearly established.

VP004.observation: People and scene stay recognizable, unlike R16A full-screen stripes. The distorted horizontal object at chest height is already present in the initial frame and also in B400/B400+I; this is not evidence of newly generated full-screen stripes. Motion is limited and neither bending until cracking nor a propagating fracture is clearly shown.

VP009.observation: Worker stands and moves out of frame; glass panel remains in place. No clear suction-cup lifting of the glass, and the cup appears detached from the intended glass interaction. No A-style full-frame stripe collapse in the inspected samples.

conclusion: The three previously catastrophic examples no longer exhibit full-frame stripe collapse in these sampled R16B frames. Physical/semantic process failures remain. This is partial visual improvement, not evidence that all visual/PC/SA/Joint goals are met.
